LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_StatusTip: The loaded world's border-development mode is stored in that save. The new-world default applies when BOTR first initializes another world.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_SettlementScopeNote: Hierarchy changes apply to political settlement roles. Physical-map options affect eligible non-player settlement maps generated after the option is enabled; already saved maps are not rebuilt.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_OverlayTip: Display faction-colored territory and boundary lines on the world map.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_OpacityTip: Controls how strongly faction colors tint the world map.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_LegacyTerritoryTip: Specialized compatibility defaults used only when BOTR first initializes an already-established world. Most players should leave these unchanged.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_InfluenceRadiusTip: Base distance that each settlement projects political control when Borders of the Rim initializes an established save. New evolving-frontier worlds use their maturation setting instead.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_ConnectTerritoriesTip: When an established save is initialized, expands isolated non-player claims toward a nearby settlement of the same faction. New evolving-frontier worlds do not force starting connections.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_NeutralBoundaryTip: When an established save is initialized, leaves equally influenced starting tiles unclaimed. Evolving frontiers use fixed shared borders after contact.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableSettlementHierarchyT: Assign capitals, major settlements, standard settlements, and outposts. Tiers change influence reach, military strength, defense, mission value, and—when enabled below—the physical settlement map. Capitals also receive a crown on the political map. Existing saves are supported.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableTieredSettlementMaps: Scale generated settlement maps by tier

Keep each faction's normal settlement generator and augment newly visited sites by tier. Outposts remain compact, settlements gain a satellite district, major centers become larger and fortified, and capitals become multi-district strongholds. The two options below add identity and political-state details. Disable this compatibility option if another mod requires complete control of settlement maps.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableFactionSignatureSite: Add tier-scaled landmarks and facilities associated with tribal, civil, militarist, Imperial, waster, pigskin, Yttakin, and general industrial factions. Unknown modded factions receive a technology-appropriate fallback.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnablePoliticalSettlementV: Reflect political conditions on settlement maps

Change defenders, defenses, supplies, civic features, and building condition when a generated site is at war, occupied, unstable, prosperous, a coalition seat, a subject capital, or suffering supply disruption.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_SettlementSizeDiversityTip: Controls how many non-capital settlements become major centers or outposts. At zero, non-capital settlements remain uniform. The default 65% provides useful variety whenever a faction controls enough settlements.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_BorderNotificationsTip: Notify you when a player caravan enters or leaves faction-controlled territory.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnforceTrespassingTip: Neutral factions warn caravans without recognized passage and eventually apply goodwill penalties. Allies and caravans traveling to that faction's settlement have passage.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_GraceDaysTip: How long a caravan may remain in neutral territory after a warning before goodwill is lost.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_GoodwillPenaltyTip: Goodwill lost each time a caravan remains past another full grace period.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableWarsTip: Allow neighboring non-player factions to declare territorial wars, fight simulated battles, and capture settlements.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_WarNewsTip: Show letters and messages for declarations, offensives, captures, and peace settlements.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_VisibleRaidForcesTip: Make Borders of the Rim territorial battles, player-campaign counterattacks, and autonomous-colony threats travel across the world before resolving. Vanilla, quest, drop-pod, mechanoid, and other mods' raids are not delayed or replaced.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MaxWarsTip: Limits how many territorial wars can be simulated at once.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_WarFrequencyTip: Controls how often neighboring factions consider starting a territorial war.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_BattleIntervalTip: Controls how often each active war resolves an off-screen battle.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableCoalitionsTip: Allow neighboring non-player factions with compatible interests or shared enemies to form persistent alliances, expand them, and support members that are attacked.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableDependenciesTip: Allow decisive wars to create vassal states and weaker factions to seek voluntary protection from stronger neighbors. Subjects retain their settlements and faction identity.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableTerritorialDiplomacy: Allow stronger factions to demand exposed settlements and compatible neighbors to negotiate mutually beneficial enclave exchanges. Refused demands may escalate into territorial wars.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableCivilWars: Enable stability, rebellions, and faction collapse
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableCivilWarsTip: Track internal stability for non-player factions. Severe exhaustion, defeat, territorial losses, or rising vassal autonomy can produce independence wars, secessionist factions, civil wars, and government collapse.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MinimumRebellionSettlement: Minimum settlements for a faction split: {0}
A faction must control at least this many settlements before an internal rebellion can split off a new faction. Vassal independence wars do not use this limit.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnablePlayerRecognitionTip: Allow the colony to build political standing, proclaim sovereignty, earn recognition from foreign governments, negotiate recognized passage, and receive improved territorial mission terms.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_PlayerRecognitionThreshold: Political standing required before the colony may proclaim itself a sovereign territorial state. Standing comes from territory, population, diplomacy, completed war missions, and time survived.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_PoliticalNewsTip: Show letters for coalition developments and foreign recognition of the player's state.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MaxCoalitionSizeTip: Limits the number of factions that may belong to one defensive coalition.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_PoliticalFrequencyTip: Controls how often factions consider forming or expanding coalitions.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableMissionsTip: Allow non-hostile factions in active territorial wars to request direct player intervention.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MissionFrequencyTip: Controls the interval between opportunities to intervene in territorial wars.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MissionThreatTip: Scales the strength of counterattacks generated by hold-frontier missions.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MissionRewardTip: Scales silver payments for successful territorial missions.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_ClusterRadiusTip: Baseline radius for spreading settlements throughout a faction homeland. Defaults to 120 and can be adjusted from 12 to 240 tiles. Highly populated factions may expand to the configured limit to preserve useful spacing. This only affects newly generated worlds.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_LayoutVariationTip: Adds natural variation to faction homeland compactness, settlement distance from the capital, and spacing between settlements. Higher values strengthen deterministic compact, elongated, twin-lobed, frontier-arm, and broad/scattered homeland profiles while preserving connected own-side placement. Defaults to 35%. This only affects newly generated worlds.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_TerritoryShapeVariationTip: Shapes progressive expansion with broad faction-specific geographic currents and restrained resistance from hills and mountains. Higher values create larger lobes, indentations, and more distinctive mature territories without adding disconnected random noise. Defaults to 35%. The selected value is fixed when a world first initializes Borders of the Rim.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_FullyEstablishedBorders: Default new worlds to fully established borders
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_FullyEstablishedBordersTip: New worlds—and established saves initializing Borders of the Rim for the first time—immediately receive their complete mature political territories. When an incomplete progressive BOTR save is loaded while this default is enabled, a one-time choice asks whether that save should also be completed. Border contact and tension begin immediately. Conquest, settlement changes, and political transfers can still move borders.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_ExpansionYearsTip: How long progressive borders take to spread across all reachable inhabited land when fully established borders are disabled. Fresh worlds target first contact around day 30–45; established worlds immediately recognize borders that already touch. RimWorld years are 60 days.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_CompleteCurrentWorldTip: Permanently advances the currently loaded Borders of the Rim world to its complete mature political map.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_CompleteCurrentWorldConfir:
Complete territorial expansion in the currently loaded world?
All mature faction borders will be established immediately. Border contact and political tension will begin wherever those territories touch. This cannot restore the previous frontier state without loading an earlier save.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_CompleteCurrentWorldSucces: Territorial expansion completed. This world now uses fully established borders.
LanguageData.BOTR_FullyEstablishedPrompt_Title: Border development differs from your current setting
LanguageData.BOTR_FullyEstablishedPrompt_Text:
This world currently uses progressive territorial expansion, but Borders of the Rim is now configured to default to fully established borders.
Would you like to complete this world's territorial expansion now? All mature faction borders will be established immediately, and political tension will begin wherever territories touch. This cannot restore the previous frontier state without loading an earlier save.
LanguageData.BOTR_FullyEstablishedPrompt_ProgressiveK: This world will continue using progressive territorial expansion.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_NewWorldNote: Homeland placement requires a newly generated world. When added to an established save, Borders of the Rim preserves every settlement location and current political claim, then uses the selected frontier-development mode for expansion into wilderness.
LanguageData.BOTR_EstablishedMigration_SuccessLabel: Borders of the Rim initialized successfully
LanguageData.BOTR_EstablishedMigration_SuccessText:
Borders of the Rim has been integrated into this established world.
• {0} eligible settlements across {1} factions initialized • {2} starting political claim tiles retained • Territory, hierarchy, diplomacy, war, mission, caravan, raid, and support systems initialized
No settlement was relocated, transferred, or regenerated. Existing settlement positions define the starting political map, and factions will expand into reachable wilderness over approximately {3} RimWorld year(s). Borders that already touch become active political contacts immediately; other factions will make contact as their frontiers grow.
LanguageData.BOTR_EstablishedMigration_FullyEstablish:
Borders of the Rim has been integrated into this established world.
• {0} eligible settlements across {1} factions initialized • {2} starting political claim tiles retained • Territory, hierarchy, diplomacy, war, mission, caravan, raid, and support systems initialized
No settlement was relocated, transferred, or regenerated. Existing settlement positions define the political map, and complete mature borders have been established immediately. Factions that now share borders begin as active political contacts; conquest, settlement changes, and political transfers can still move those borders.
LanguageData.BOTR_Message_FirstBorderContact: {0} and {1} have made first territorial contact. Their shared frontier is now disputed.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_BorderTensionTip: Political friction along a shared frontier. Relations and political events change tension over time. At 30 tension, factions may issue territorial demands. At 70 tension, eligible factions may declare war.
LanguageData.BOTR_TerritoryRole_Occupied: Occupied territory; formerly controlled by {0} ({1} day(s) until consolidation)
LanguageData.BOTR_TerritoryRole_Demanded: Subject to an active territorial demand from {0}
LanguageData.BOTR_TerritoryRole_DoesNotRecognizePlaye: Does not recognize the player's sovereignty
LanguageData.BOTR_SettlementMapProfile_Settlement: native-faction base with a satellite district
LanguageData.BOTR_WorldToggle_Tip: Toggle the Borders of the Rim political territory overlay.
LanguageData.BOTR_World_PlayerStatusTip: Political standing: {0}/{1}. Foreign recognition: {2}/{3} governments required.
LanguageData.BOTR_World_ActiveWarsTip: Open the territorial-war overview, inspect each conflict, or jump directly to its front and objective.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_None: There are no active territorial wars.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_Summary: Active conflicts: {0}. Hover over any field for details.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_AttackerTip: {0} began this conflict and currently holds the offensive initiative.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_DefenderTip: {0} is defending its territory in this conflict.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_TerritorialWarTip: A conventional border war. Simulated battles build momentum and exhaustion, and exposed settlements may change hands.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_CivilWarTip: An internal struggle between a government and a breakaway faction. Victory may reunify the state or establish a separate government.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_IndependenceWarTip: A subject government is fighting its former overlord for political independence.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_PlayerCampaignTip: A player-led territorial campaign. You must personally secure its objectives; background simulation cannot capture them for you.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_DurationTip: Elapsed time since this conflict began.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_ObjectiveTip: The settlement currently exposed to attack. Capturing it advances the war and moves the front deeper into enemy territory.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_CapturesTip: {0} has captured this many settlements during the current war.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_NextBattleTip: Estimated time until the next background battle is resolved. Political activity and player missions can alter the conflict before then.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_CampaignStatusTip: The current step required to advance your player-led campaign.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_CounteroffensiveTip: The defender's scheduled response to your campaign. Enemy attacks pause while campaign terms are awaiting your decision.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_ObjectivesSecuredTip: Settlements permanently secured during this campaign, compared with the maximum allowed in one offensive.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_LeverageTip: Your negotiating position. Secured objectives and campaign performance can improve the terms available to you.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_JumpFrontTip: Center the world camera on the current contact point between these factions.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_JumpFrontUnavailable: This conflict does not currently have a valid visible front.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_JumpObjectiveTip: Center the world camera on this conflict's current strategic objective.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_JumpObjectiveUnavailabl: This conflict does not currently have an available settlement objective.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarOverview_TermsTip: Review the available choices for continuing, settling, or withdrawing from your campaign.
LanguageData.BOTR_VisibleRaid_StatusWaiting: At the destination; preparing to engage
LanguageData.BOTR_VisibleRaid_CampaignLaunchText:
{0} has dispatched a military force from {1} toward {2} in response to your territorial campaign.
The warband is visible on the world map and is expected to arrive in approximately {3} day(s). If {2} is a loaded colony, its arrival will begin a real raid. If it is an autonomous colony, its arrival will begin that holding's normal defense crisis.
LanguageData.BOTR_VisibleRaid_AutonomousLaunchText:
{0} has dispatched a military force from {1} toward the autonomous colony of {2}.
The force is visible on the world map and is expected to arrive in approximately {3} day(s). The autonomous-colony defense decision will become available if the force reaches the holding.
LanguageData.BOTR_VisibleRaid_CampaignAbortedText: {0}'s moving force reached {1}, but another active threat or an invalid tactical state prevented the counterattack from deploying. After waiting for two days, the force withdrew without creating a second overlapping raid.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_StatusActive: Objective {1}/{2}: capture {0}, then annex it directly or establish an autonomous colony.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_StatusSettlement: {0} is secured. Choose campaign terms before proceeding. Objectives secured: {1}/{2}.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_StatusUnavailable: The claimed objective is no longer available.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_CounterattackPaused: Paused while campaign terms are pending.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_Duration:
Duration: {0} days
This campaign advances only through your direct assault; it is never resolved by the background battle simulator.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ClaimCommandDesc: Declare a player-led territorial campaign for this exposed settlement. The target faction becomes hostile and the campaign remains active until you settle terms or withdraw.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_Confirm:
Declare a territorial campaign against {1} for control of {0}?
This immediately begins hostilities. You must personally defeat the settlement and then annex it directly or establish an autonomous colony to secure the claim. Afterward, you may consolidate, demand reparations, or press toward another connected objective, up to three per campaign. Background battles cannot complete these objectives for you, but the defender will launch counterattacks against your nearby holdings.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_WithdrawConfirm:
Withdraw your claim to {0} and end the territorial campaign against {1}?
Peace will be restored where possible, but abandoning the claim costs {2} goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_Disabled: Faction wars are disabled in the mod settings.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_NoTerritory: You need at least one player-controlled settlement before making a territorial claim.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_InvalidTarget: This settlement cannot be claimed through a territorial campaign.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_AlreadyActive: Only one player offensive campaign may be active at a time.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_AlliedTarget: {0} is allied with you. End the alliance before making a territorial claim.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_TargetCommitted: {0} is already committed to another territorial war.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_NoSharedBorder: Your territory does not yet share a border with {0}.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_TargetReserved: This settlement is currently loaded or reserved by another political event.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_NoExposedTarget: This faction has no available exposed settlement to claim.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_NotFrontierTarget: {0} is the faction's current accessible front-line settlement and must be claimed first.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_HostilityFailed: Hostilities with {0} could not be established.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_DeclaredText:
You have declared a territorial campaign against {0}. Capture {1} and choose direct annexation or autonomous government to secure its land. You will then decide whether to settle or continue the offensive.
The sword and shield on the world map mark your offensive settlement and the defended objective. This campaign will not advance through simulated battles. Expect the first enemy counterattack in roughly 9–14 days.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ObjectiveSecuredText:
{0} is now under your control. You have secured {1} of at most {2} objectives in this campaign.
Enemy counteroffensives are paused while you decide whether to consolidate, demand reparations, or press the offensive. This decision remains available under Active Wars → Campaign terms if you dismiss this letter.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_EscalatedText: You have pressed the offensive toward {0}, objective {1} of {2}. The defender is mobilizing quickly; expect its next counterattack in roughly 6–10 days.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_AutonomousCounteratt: {0} has answered your territorial claim with a counterattack against the autonomous colony at {1}.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ColonyRaidText: {0} has answered your territorial campaign with a direct raid on {1}. This is a strategic counterattack intended to force your offensive to collapse.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_VictoryText: Your conquest of {0} has secured the claim against {1}. The campaign has ended, political borders and standing have been recalculated, and peace has been restored where possible.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_RazedText: You razed {0} instead of taking political control from {1}. The campaign has ended without gaining that settlement or its territory.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_RelinquishedText: You transferred {0} rather than taking it from {1} for your own government. The player campaign has ended without securing the claim.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_WithdrawnText: You abandoned the claim to {0}. The campaign against {1} has ended, though the failed offensive has damaged relations.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_DefenderCollapsedTex: The campaign for {0} ended because {1} can no longer sustain a government.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ObjectiveLostText: The campaign ended because {0} is no longer controlled by {1}. Active objectives are never silently retargeted.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_DefeatText: The campaign for {0} has collapsed after {1}'s counteroffensive eliminated every player-controlled settlement. The claim has been abandoned.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_DecisiveVictoryText: Your capture of {0} left {1} without a functioning territorial government. The campaign has ended in decisive victory and borders have been recalculated.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_TermsActiveIntro: Your offensive for {0} is still active. You may continue the assault, purchase an early ceasefire, or withdraw without terms.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_TermsSettlementIntro: You have secured {0}. Choose how to convert that victory into a political settlement.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_TermsRecoverable: You may close this window and return at any time through Active Wars → Campaign terms.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ConsolidateDesc: End the campaign with the settlements already secured and restore peace where the opposing faction permits it.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ConsolidatedText: You consolidated your capture of {0} and ended the campaign against {1}. Borders and political standing have been recalculated.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_DemandDesc: Use your battlefield leverage to end the campaign and receive {0} silver by cargo pod at a loaded home colony. This further damages goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_InsufficientLeverage: You need a secured objective and at least 25 player leverage to demand reparations.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ReparationsNeedColon: A loaded player home colony is required to receive reparations.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ReparationsWonText: {1} accepted your terms after the capture of {0}. {2} silver is arriving by cargo pod at {3}, and the campaign has ended.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_ContinueDesc: Escalate toward the next exposed settlement, {0}. The next enemy counterattack will arrive sooner.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_MaximumObjectives: A single campaign may secure at most {0} settlements. Consolidate or demand terms before declaring another campaign.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_NoRemainingObjective: The defender has no remaining exposed settlement available for this campaign.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_NoLongerBordering: Your territory no longer shares an active border with {0}; the offensive cannot continue.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_OfferDesc: Pay {0} silver from loaded home maps for an early ceasefire. The campaign ends and goodwill suffers a small additional penalty.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_OfferConfirm: Pay {0} silver to {1} and end this campaign immediately?
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_MissingCeasefireSilv: You need {0} accessible silver across loaded player home maps.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_PaidPeaceText: You paid {2} silver to end the campaign for {0} against {1}. Peace has been restored where possible.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_PermanentEnemyTerms: This faction cannot negotiate peace or exchange reparations.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_TermsUnavailable: Campaign terms are not available in the current state.
LanguageData.BOTR_PlayerCampaign_WithdrawDesc: End the campaign without a negotiated settlement. This costs 15 goodwill and relinquishes the current objective.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_UnclaimedDescription: No faction currently projects enough influence to control this tile. Caravans may pass freely and founding a settlement here is not a territorial intrusion.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_AccessTip: How this government treats player caravans. Allies, the player's own government, and factions that formally recognize the player permit passage. Neutral caravans may also enter to trade; otherwise lingering in neutral territory can trigger trespass warnings and goodwill penalties when enforcement is enabled. Hostile territory provides no safe passage.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StrategicWeightTip: Strength changes this settlement's contribution to simulated faction warfare. Defense changes how difficult it is to capture in simulated battles and related territorial calculations. Higher-tier settlements are strategically more valuable and better defended.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_InfluenceReachTip: Adjusts how far this settlement projects territorial control beyond the normal settlement radius. Capitals and major settlements reach farther; outposts project less influence.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_NeutralPolicy: Neutral passage is tolerated, but caravans without trade clearance receive a warning. Remaining for {0} day(s) costs {1} goodwill per enforcement period.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_EnforcementDisabled: Territorial trespassing enforcement is disabled in the mod settings.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_WarScoreTip: Measures momentum from simulated battles, settlement captures, and player intervention missions. The leading side is more likely to attack and capture exposed objectives. A lead of 70 can force the war toward settlement.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_ExhaustionTip: Accumulated strain on the attacker and defender. Battles, defeats, and missions increase exhaustion. If either side reaches 85%, the war moves toward a ceasefire or political settlement.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StabilityTip: Internal political health from 0–100. Peace, coalitions, and protective political relationships improve stability; exhausting wars, defeats, recent settlement losses, and being reduced to one settlement lower it. Stable: 70–100. Strained: 50–69. Unstable: 30–49. Crisis: below 30. Eligible factions in crisis may suffer rebellion or secession.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_RecognitionStatusTip: Your state's current political stage, progressing from frontier colony to territorial claimant, declared state, and finally a recognized power.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_PoliticalStandingTip: Combined measure of territorial control, population, diplomacy, completed territorial missions, and survival time. Reaching the displayed threshold allows you to proclaim sovereignty; continued growth helps secure foreign recognition.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_ForeignRecognitionTip: The number of eligible foreign governments that formally recognize your sovereignty. Recognition is evaluated after proclaiming a state and depends on political standing and diplomatic relationships. Reach the required count to become a recognized power.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_RecognizedByTip: Governments currently recognizing your state. Recognizing factions grant caravan passage and pay a 20% premium for their territorial missions.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StandingSourcesTip: These five sources add together to produce your political standing, up to a maximum of 100.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StandingTerritoryTip: Each player-controlled settlement provides 12 points. Claimed land provides 1 additional point per 10 tiles, up to 12 land points. Territory standing is capped at 40.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StandingPopulationTip: Each colonist on a loaded home map or in a player caravan counts toward population. Autonomous colonies contribute 2 plus their administrative level as virtual residents. The total population count provides 1.5 points per resident, capped at 20.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StandingDiplomacyTip: Each allied eligible government provides 5 points. Each eligible neutral government with at least 40 goodwill provides 2 points. Diplomacy standing is capped at 15.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StandingMissionsTip: Each completed Borders of the Rim territorial mission provides 3 points. Mission standing is capped at 15.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_StandingLongevityTip: Your state gains approximately 1 point for every 12 in-game days survived. Longevity standing is capped at 10 after 120 days.
LanguageData.BOTR_Tab_RecognitionBenefits: Signatory governments grant caravan passage and pay a 20% premium on territorial war missions.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_NoLongerAvailable: This mission is no longer available.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_CannotAccept: The factions involved can no longer support this intervention.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_CannotBetrayAlly: This contract is no longer available because {0} is allied with your government.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_WarEntryConfirm:
Enter the war?
Accepting this contract will bring your government into {0}'s war against {1}. {1} will become hostile. Continue?
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_WarEntryHomeConfirm:
Enter the war?
Accepting this contract will bring your government into {0}'s war against {1}. {1} will become hostile and attack {2} in approximately six hours. Continue?
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_ConsequencesNewHostility:
Diplomatic consequences:
• Accepting this contract will bring your government into {0}'s war against {1}.
• {1} will become hostile.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_ConsequencesExistingHostili:
Diplomatic consequences:
• Accepting this contract will bring your government into {0}'s war against {1}.
• {1} is already hostile.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_ConsequencesHomeAttack: \n• {0} will attack {1} in approximately six hours.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_CaptureOfferLabel: Mission: capture the command center at {0}
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_CaptureOfferText: {0} is requesting direct intervention in its territorial war against {1}. Assault {2} and destroy the hardened command center that appears when the settlement map is generated. The mission must be completed within 12 days.\n\nDestroying the command center will give {0} a major advantage and exhaust {1}'s war effort. Payment: {3} silver, plus goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_DefendOfferLabel: Contract: open a second front at {0}
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_DefendOfferText: {0} has captured territory from {1} and expects a counterattack. They are offering payment for your colony at {2} to openly enter the conflict as a diversionary front, drawing enemy forces away from the occupation. If accepted, you will receive approximately six hours to prepare before the counterattack. Hold the colony for one day and eliminate the attackers.\n\nPayment: {3} silver, plus goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_SiegeOfferLabel: Contract: draw out an enemy siege at {0}
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_SiegeOfferText: {0} wants your colony at {2} to enter its war against {1} and draw enemy siege forces away from the territorial front. If accepted, {1} will establish siege lines around the colony in approximately six hours. Destroy or drive off the besieging force before the five-day deadline.\n\nBreaking the siege will damage {1}'s war effort. Payment: {3} silver, plus goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_SabotageOfferLabel: Mission: sabotage the supply depot at {0}
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_SabotageOfferText: {0} has located a forward supply depot supporting {1}'s campaign at {2}. Assault the settlement and destroy the marked depot within 12 days.\n\nSuccess will disrupt {1}'s supply strength in simulated battles for five days. Payment: {3} silver, plus goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_EscortOfferText: {0} needs a four-person military convoy escorted across your colony map at {2} while {1} attempts an interception. The convoy arrives in six hours. At least three members must reach the opposite edge alive.\n\nPayment: {3} silver, plus goodwill.
LanguageData.BOTR_Mission_OccupiedDefendOfferText: {0} has seized {2} from {1}, but the occupation is vulnerable. Send a caravan to the settlement within six days, enter its map, and help repel the counterattack while holding the site for one day.\n\nPayment: {3} silver, plus goodwill.

LanguageData.BOTR_Coalition_ReasonSecurity: Both governments seek greater regional security.
LanguageData.BOTR_Coalition_ReasonThreat: The shared threat posed by {0} accelerated the agreement.

LanguageData.BOTR_IndependenceWar_IndependentText: {0}'s rebellion against {1} ended without renewed submission. The former vassal remains an independent territorial power.
LanguageData.BOTR_Collapse_Text: {0} can no longer sustain a territorial government. {1}
LanguageData.BOTR_Collapse_NoSuccessor: No single successor has inherited its remaining political claims.
LanguageData.BOTR_Collapse_Successor: {0} has absorbed its final stronghold and emerged as the successor government.

Existing allies and governments whose wars you have supported will be the most likely to recognize the new state.

LanguageData.BOTR_Recognition_ForeignText: {0} has formally recognized {1} as a sovereign territorial state. Relations improve by 5 goodwill. Its territory now grants your caravans recognized passage, and its territorial war contracts pay a 20% diplomatic premium.
LanguageData.BOTR_Recognition_AchievedLabel: Your state is a recognized territorial power
LanguageData.BOTR_Recognition_AchievedText: Enough foreign governments now recognize {0} for its sovereign status to be politically established across the rim. Your state will permanently be regarded as an independent territorial power.\n\nRecognizing governments: {1}.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_DeclarationText: {0} has declared a territorial war against {1}. Its first strategic objective is {2}. Crossed swords mark the attacking settlement and a shield marks the defended objective on the world map.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_CaptureText: {0} has seized {2} from {1}. The settlement and its surrounding territory are now under occupation.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_PeaceCollapse: The conflict ended after one belligerent could no longer sustain a government.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_PeaceNoObjectives: The conflict ended because no viable strategic objectives remained.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_PeaceFinalStronghold: The offensive stopped short of eliminating the defender's final settlement.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_PeaceExhaustion: Mounting losses and war exhaustion forced negotiations.
LanguageData.BOTR_WarNews_PeaceStalemate: The result was a military stalemate.
LanguageData.BOTR_Message_EnteredAlliedTerritory: {0} has entered allied territory controlled by {1}.

LanguageData.BOTR_Message_EnteredNeutralTerritory: {0} has entered territory controlled by {1} without recognized passage.
LanguageData.BOTR_Message_TrespassPenalty: {0} ignored {1}'s border warning. Goodwill decreased by {2}.
LanguageData.BOTR_Letter_BorderWarningText: {0} has formally warned that {1} is traveling through its territory without recognized passage. LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_Introduction: Your forces have defeated the defenders of {0}, formerly controlled by {1}. RimWorld would normally erase the settlement now; Borders of the Rim preserves it while you decide its fate.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_SponsoredIntroduction: Your forces have defeated the defenders of {0}, formerly controlled by {1}. This assault was undertaken for {2}, which expects the settlement to be transferred. Keeping or razing it will be treated as a betrayal.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_AnnexDesc: Take direct control of the loaded map, its surviving structures, and its territory. This becomes a normal player colony and counts against RimWorld's colony limit.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_AutonomousDesc: Keep the settlement and its territory under local administration without consuming a player-colony slot. Choose one specialization; it will send scheduled support to a loaded colony.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_AutonomousSponsoredDesc: Keep the settlement under local administration instead of transferring it to {0}. It will not consume a player-colony slot, but the sponsor will regard this as a betrayal.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_ColonyLimit: Full annexation is unavailable because RimWorld's colony limit is currently {0}. Raise that limit in the game options or choose another outcome.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_TransferDesc: Honor the contract and give {0} permanent control. {1}
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_RazeDesc: Use RimWorld's normal defeated-settlement outcome. The settlement is permanently removed and the land becomes available for changing borders.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_RazeSponsoredDesc: Destroy the settlement instead of transferring it to {0}. The sponsor will regard this as a betrayal.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_MustDecide: The game remains paused until the settlement's ownership is decided.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_DecideCommandDesc: Choose whether this conquered settlement will be directly annexed, governed autonomously, transferred to its sponsor, or razed.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_PendingInspect: Conquered: awaiting the player's ownership decision.

LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_NoLongerAvailable: This settlement is no longer awaiting a conquest decision.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_SponsorUnavailable: The sponsoring faction can no longer receive this settlement.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_AnnexedText: {0} is now a fully controlled player colony. Its loaded map remains intact, it counts against RimWorld's colony limit, and its territory has joined your political borders.

LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_DepartureGravship: Launch your gravship and withdraw any remaining forces when ready.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_DepartureGeneric: Withdraw your expedition from the conquered map when ready. Reform a caravan or use another available transport method.
LanguageData.BOTR_Conquest_BetrayalText: You refused to transfer the conquered settlement to {0}. Any active capture contract has failed, and goodwill with the sponsor has fallen sharply.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_SelectIntro: Autonomous colonies hold territory and contribute virtual population without remaining loaded. Each normally schedules specialized support every 15 days for your preferred loaded home colony. Loaded battlefields, defense crises, gravship servicing, or an unavailable home can delay delivery.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_CharterCaravanRemains: The caravan's pawns and all supplies not included in the founding cost remain together on the world map.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_CharterConfirm:
Charter {0} as a level 1 {1} autonomous colony?
This consumes {2} from the caravan. The caravan itself remains intact.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_CharterSurfaceOnly: Autonomous colonies can only be chartered on the planet's surface.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_CharteredText:
Your caravan spent {3} to establish {0}, a level 1 {1} autonomous colony. Its current scheduled support is {2}.
The holding immediately contributes territory and virtual population without consuming a normal colony slot. Your caravan remains on the tile and may depart normally. Hostile factions may threaten the colony after its initial 45–75 day grace period.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_AgrarianDesc: Farms, preserves, and distributes durable food for the wider state. Level 1 output: 30 packaged survival meals per scheduled shipment.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_IndustrialDesc: Operates mines and workshops that supply construction materials. Level 1 output: 180 steel and 4 components per scheduled shipment.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_CommercialDesc: Coordinates regional trade and returns tax revenue. Level 1 output: 300 silver per scheduled shipment.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_MilitaryDesc: Maintains a fortified garrison and supplies field medicine. Level 1 output: 12 industrial medicine per scheduled shipment.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_AgrarianOutput: {0} packaged survival meals per scheduled shipment
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_IndustrialOutput: {0} steel and {1} components per scheduled shipment
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_EstablishedText: {0} is now a level 1 {1} autonomous colony. It immediately holds the settlement's territory without consuming a normal colony slot. Its current support is {2}.\n\n{3} After all blocking pawns and objects depart, the battlefield will unload while the autonomous settlement remains on the world map. Hostile factions may threaten the holding after an initial 45–75 day grace period.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_ManageDesc: Review this holding's specialization, support schedule, and direct-control option.
LanguageData.BOTR_SupportDestination_Tip: The state-wide destination for autonomous shipments, territorial mission payments, and campaign reparations. If the preferred home is unavailable, the first available loaded player home receives the delivery instead.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_ShipmentText: {0} has dispatched its scheduled support: {1}. Cargo pods carrying the supplies are arriving at {2}.

Stock is persistent and refreshes every 30 days. Administrative level increases stock quantities; specialization determines the market's focus, while Commercial colonies carry more silver and offer the best internal prices. Trading does not consume or delay scheduled support shipments.
LanguageData.BOTR_AutonomousTrade_Unavailable: That autonomous colony cannot trade right now.
LanguageData.BOTR_AutonomousTrade_LoadedMap: Trading is unavailable while this holding's tactical map is loaded.
LanguageData.BOTR_AutonomousTrade_DefenseCrisis: Resolve this holding's defense crisis before trading.
LanguageData.BOTR_AutonomousTrade_PlayerCaravanRequir: A player-controlled caravan is required to trade here.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_NoLongerAvailable: This autonomous colony is no longer available.

LanguageData.BOTR_GravshipService_LoadedMapStatus: Unavailable while the holding's tactical map is loaded

LanguageData.BOTR_GravshipService_WaitingInspect: Awaiting an onward destination after autonomous-colony servicing.
LanguageData.BOTR_GravshipService_NoLongerWaiting: This gravship is no longer waiting at an autonomous-colony service stop.
LanguageData.BOTR_GravshipService_ColonyUnavailable: The servicing autonomous colony is no longer available.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_UpgradeMaximum: This colony has reached the maximum administrative level of 3.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_UpgradeWaitForUnload: The conquered battlefield must unload before this colony can be upgraded.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_UpgradeDuringCrisis: Resolve the active defense crisis before upgrading this colony.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_UpgradeMissingResources: Insufficient accessible resources in loaded player homes. {0}.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_UpgradePaymentChanged: The available resources changed before the upgrade could be paid.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseLocalChanceTip: The chance that the autonomous colony's local garrison would defeat an attack without player intervention or paid reinforcements. Administrative level, military specialization, original settlement tier, and attacker strength affect this value.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseRespondDesc: Choose whether to reinforce the local garrison, defend this holding personally, or trust its existing defenses.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseSecureNext: Secure; next threat check in about {0} day(s)
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseThreatText: {0} is preparing an assault on the autonomous colony at {1}. You have {2} days to respond.\n\nThe local garrison currently has a {3}% chance to hold. Spending {4} silver on reinforcements raises this to {5}%. Ignoring the warning reduces it to {6}%. You may instead send a caravan and fight the attack personally.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseWindowIntro: {0} is moving against this holding. Choose a response before the deadline: {1}.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseReinforceDesc: Deduct the silver from loaded player homes and resolve the assault abstractly with a {0}% chance to hold.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseNeedsColonist: A caravan needs at least one living, healthy, free colonist to defend this holding personally.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseLocalDesc: Spend nothing and resolve the assault abstractly in one day with a {0}% chance to hold.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseIgnoredDesc: If no response is chosen before the deadline, the unsupported garrison will defend with only a {0}% chance to hold.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseNoLongerAvailable: This defense decision is no longer available.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseMissingSilver: This response requires {0} accessible silver in loaded player homes.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefensePaymentChanged: The available silver changed before reinforcements could be funded.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseMapFailed: The temporary defense map could not be generated. No defense response was consumed.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseSiteReady: {0}'s level {1} {2} settlement and its {3}-member local garrison are ready for the approaching attack.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseAssetProtected: This belongs to the autonomous colony and cannot be dismantled or removed.
LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseRaidPreparingText: {0} has detected your caravan and the local garrison at {1}. The enemy assault will reach the colony in six hours.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseWonPersonalText: Your forces defeated {1}'s assault on {0}. Reform the caravan and leave when ready; the tactical map will unload and autonomous operation will resume.

LanguageData.BOTR_Autonomous_DefenseCancelledText: The attacking faction can no longer continue its assault on {0}. The defense crisis has ended without a battle or loss.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_EnableFactionCaravansTip: Non-player factions send real, visible trade caravans between their own settlements. Player caravans can intercept them to trade peacefully or attack them.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_MaxFactionCaravansTip: Limits how many intercity faction caravans may exist across the world at once. At most one caravan from each faction is active.
LanguageData.BOTR_Settings_FactionCaravanFrequencyTip: Changes how often the world tries to launch a new intercity caravan. Normal frequency is roughly one attempt every 4–7 days after an initial 5–9 day delay.
LanguageData.BOTR_FactionCaravan_NoLongerAvailable: This faction caravan is no longer available.
LanguageData.BOTR_FactionCaravan_AlreadyIntercepted: Another player caravan is already intercepting this caravan.
LanguageData.BOTR_FactionCaravan_PlayerRequired: Only a player-controlled caravan can intercept this caravan.
LanguageData.BOTR_FactionCaravan_MeetingText: {0} has intercepted {1}, a caravan of {2} traveling from {3} to {4}. You may trade if relations permit, attack the caravan, or let it continue on its route.
LanguageData.BOTR_FactionCaravan_AmbushConfirm: Attack {0}? This is an unprovoked attack on {1}. It will make the faction hostile and generate a real caravan battlefield.
LanguageData.BOTR_FactionCaravan_AmbushStarted: You have attacked a caravan belonging to {0}.
